Sita. The virtuous princess and wife of Rama in the great Hindu epic the Ramayana, whose abduction by the demon-king Ravana sets the entire story in motion. Her rescue becomes the defining heroic quest of Hanuman, and her steadfast devotion through trials establishes her as an icon of feminine virtue and loyalty in Hindu culture.

Sita was born from the earth itself as a divine gift to King Janaka. Her name means furrow, and she became renowned for her beauty, intelligence, and unwavering virtue, establishing her as an ideal of womanhood in Hindu thought. She married Rama in a swayamvara, a contest where she chose him from among assembled princes. Their union was idealized as a perfect partnership, though their relationship would be tested by separation and scandal.

When Rama and his brother Lakshman were exiled to the forest for fourteen years, Sita went with them. The ten-headed demon-king Ravana of Lanka saw Sita and became obsessed with her. He abducted her, taking her across the ocean to his island fortress. Hanuman, the devoted follower of Rama, undertook a heroic journey to Lanka to find her. He crossed the ocean, infiltrated Ravana's palace, discovered Sita in captivity, and reported back to Rama. Hanuman's quest became the pivot of the entire narrative.

Throughout her captivity, Sita endured alone and far from home. She refused Ravana's advances and maintained her complete fidelity to Rama. Her steadfast virtue during this trial was central to her characterization.

After Rama defeated and killed Ravana in battle, he rescued Sita. But he questioned her fidelity after her long captivity among Ravana. Sita was forced to undergo an agni pariksha, an ordeal by fire, to prove her purity. This troubling moment has generated centuries of interpretation and debate.

Sita represents dharma, the principle of righteousness, and embodies feminine virtue in Hindu ethics. Her story has been performed, recited, and celebrated across India for thousands of years, profoundly influencing ideals of motherhood, wifehood, and devoted love.
